description: A method or function that is too long to understand at a glance. Usually exceeds 30–40 lines of executable code.
detection_signal: Function body > 40 lines; cyclomatic complexity > 10; more than 3 levels of nesting
why_bad: Long methods are hard to test, understand, and change without introducing side effects. They often hide multiple responsibilities.
fix: Extract sub-functions using the Extract Method refactoring. Each function should do exactly one thing and fit on one screen.

description: A class that has too many fields, methods, or lines of code. Often a sign that the class is doing too much.
detection_signal: Class > 200 lines; > 10 instance variables; > 20 methods
why_bad: Large classes are hard to navigate, test, and understand. They violate the Single Responsibility Principle.
fix: Apply Extract Class to move groups of related fields and methods to a new class. Split by responsibility.

description: A method that takes too many parameters (typically more than 3–4).
detection_signal: Method signature has > 4 parameters
why_bad: Long parameter lists are hard to remember, easy to call in wrong order, and often indicate missing abstraction.
fix: Group related parameters into a Parameter Object (a simple dataclass/struct). Or use method chaining / builder pattern.

description: Groups of data items that always appear together (e.g., city/state/zip or start/end/step) but are not encapsulated in an object.
detection_signal: Same 3+ parameters appearing together in multiple method signatures; same field groups in multiple classes
why_bad: Clumped data is harder to refactor when the shape changes. Logic that operates on the group ends up scattered.
fix: Extract the clump into a class or named tuple. Move methods that operate on the data into that class.

description: Using primitive types (strings, ints, booleans) instead of small objects for domain concepts like Money, Phone, DateRange.
detection_signal: 'amount: float' instead of 'Money'; 'phone: str' instead of 'PhoneNumber'; magic strings as type discriminators
why_bad: Primitives have no behaviour and no validation. The same validation logic gets duplicated wherever the primitive is used.
fix: Create a small Value Object class for the concept. Put validation and formatting in that class.

description: A switch/match/if-elif chain that dispatches on a type or state discriminator, typically repeated in multiple places.
detection_signal: switch/match on an enum or type tag; same if-elif chain in multiple methods
why_bad: When new cases are added, every switch must be updated. Easy to miss one, causing silent logic bugs.
fix: Replace with polymorphism: create a class hierarchy where each subclass implements the varying behaviour.

description: An instance variable that is only set and used in certain circumstances, remaining null or default the rest of the time.
detection_signal: Field is only assigned inside a specific method, not in __init__/constructor; field is frequently null-checked before use
why_bad: Readers must understand when the field is valid and when it's garbage. Creates confusing object state.
fix: Extract the algorithm that uses the temporary fields into a separate class (Extract Class). Pass data as parameters instead.

description: A subclass that inherits methods and data from its parent but doesn't use or want most of them.
detection_signal: Subclass overrides most parent methods to throw NotImplementedError; subclass only uses 1–2 of the inherited methods
why_bad: Inheritance implies an is-a relationship. If the subclass refuses most of the contract, the hierarchy is wrong.
fix: Replace inheritance with delegation (composition). The subclass should hold an instance of the parent rather than extend it.

description: A class that needs to be modified for multiple different kinds of changes — adding a new feature touches multiple methods for unrelated reasons.
detection_signal: The same class is modified in every sprint for unrelated features; class has methods from several different domains
why_bad: Violates Single Responsibility Principle. Increases merge conflicts and regression risk.
fix: Split the class into multiple classes, each with a single responsibility. Apply Extract Class.

description: A single change requires making many small edits in many different classes.
detection_signal: Grep for a constant or field and find it copied across 5+ files; removing a feature requires touching many files
why_bad: It's easy to miss one location, leaving the system inconsistent. Changes are risky and tedious.
fix: Consolidate the scattered logic using Move Method / Move Field to put it in one place.

description: Every time you add a subclass in one hierarchy, you're forced to add a corresponding subclass in another.
detection_signal: Two class hierarchies with the same naming prefix (e.g., ShapeRenderer + ShapeEditor for each Shape subtype)
why_bad: Doubles the maintenance cost of every new type. Easy to get out of sync.
fix: Merge one hierarchy into the other, or use the Visitor pattern so behaviour is centralised.

description: Code that is never executed — unreachable branches, unused variables, commented-out blocks, or methods never called.
detection_signal: Variable assigned but never read; method exists but zero callers; code after a return statement; always-false condition
why_bad: Dead code misleads readers into thinking it's relevant. It accumulates technical debt and may contain outdated logic.
fix: Delete it. Version control preserves the history if it's ever needed again.

description: The same or very similar code structure appears in more than one place.
detection_signal: Copy-paste of 5+ identical or near-identical lines; same algorithm with minor variable name differences
why_bad: Bug fixes and enhancements must be applied in multiple places. It's easy to miss one, creating inconsistencies.
fix: Extract the duplicated code into a single function/method. Apply DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself).

description: Code written to handle future cases that don't exist yet — abstract classes with one implementation, unnecessary parameters, unused hooks.
detection_signal: Abstract class with only one concrete subclass; parameter that is always null; hook method that is never overridden
why_bad: YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It). Speculative code adds complexity without current value and may be wrong when the need arrives.
fix: Remove the unused abstraction. Refactor back to simplicity. Add the abstraction when the second use case actually appears.

description: A class that does too little to justify its existence — a thin wrapper, a class with one method, or a class that just delegates everything.
detection_signal: Class has only one non-trivial method; class only contains pass-through delegation to another class
why_bad: Every class adds cognitive overhead. A class that does nothing meaningful should be collapsed.
fix: Inline the class using Inline Class refactoring. Move its single method to the caller or target class.

description: A method that seems more interested in the data of another class than the class it belongs to.
detection_signal: Method calls many getters on another object; method would be simpler as a method of that other class
why_bad: The logic is in the wrong place, making both classes harder to understand and change independently.
fix: Move the method to the class whose data it uses most (Move Method refactoring).

description: Two classes that are too tightly coupled — each accessing the private parts of the other excessively.
detection_signal: Class A calls private/internal methods or accesses private fields of class B frequently; bidirectional dependency
why_bad: Tight coupling makes both classes impossible to change or test independently.
fix: Move shared behaviour to a third class, or use Extract Class. Limit exposure through well-defined interfaces.

description: A sequence of chained method calls: a.getB().getC().getD().doSomething() — violates the Law of Demeter.
detection_signal: Chain of 3+ method calls; train-wreck style code; breaks if any intermediate object changes its shape
why_bad: The caller is tightly coupled to the entire chain. Any change to an intermediate class breaks the chain.
fix: Apply Hide Delegate: give the first object a method that hides the chain, or restructure ownership.

description: A class that does nothing but delegate — most of its methods just call through to another object.
detection_signal: More than half of a class's methods are one-liners that delegate to another object
why_bad: The indirection adds no value. Readers must trace through the delegation to understand what actually happens.
fix: Apply Remove Middle Man: call the delegate object directly, or use Inline Class to eliminate the wrapper.

description: A class that only contains fields and getters/setters with no real behaviour — a pure data bag.
detection_signal: Class has only __init__, getters, setters, and no methods with logic; equivalent to a dict
why_bad: Logic that operates on the data ends up scattered in other classes (Feature Envy). The class can't enforce its own invariants.
fix: Move the behaviour that operates on the data into the class. Use @property and validation in __init__.

description: A single class that knows too much or does too much — controls too many other objects and contains too much logic.
detection_signal: Class > 500 lines with 30+ methods spanning multiple domains; most other classes depend on it
why_bad: The God Object becomes the bottleneck for every change. It can never be tested in isolation.
fix: Decompose using Extract Class until each class has a single, clear responsibility.

description: Domain objects are pure data structures (getters/setters only) with no business logic; all logic lives in service classes.
detection_signal: Entity/model classes have no methods beyond accessors; service classes do all the work
why_bad: Business rules are scattered across service classes, making them bloated and the domain model useless.
fix: Move business logic into the domain objects. Rich domain models encapsulate their own rules.

description: Functions or classes communicate via shared mutable global state instead of explicit parameters.
detection_signal: Use of global variables; module-level mutable singletons read/written from many places
why_bad: Global state makes execution order matter, breaks testability, and creates hidden dependencies.
fix: Pass dependencies explicitly as function parameters or constructor arguments. Use dependency injection.

description: A method that takes a boolean flag that fundamentally changes its behaviour.
detection_signal: def process(data, is_dry_run: bool) with large if/else inside; callers pass True/False literals
why_bad: Boolean flags hide what the method actually does. Callers must read the implementation to understand the effect.
fix: Split into two methods: process() and dry_run_process(). Or use an enum/strategy pattern.

description: Mixed naming conventions within the same codebase — camelCase and snake_case mixed, inconsistent abbreviations, or different names for the same concept.
detection_signal: getUserId() alongside get_user_id(); 'usr', 'user', 'account' used interchangeably for the same concept
why_bad: Inconsistency slows comprehension and causes bugs when developers assume a convention that isn't followed.
fix: Establish and enforce a naming convention via linter rules. Rename consistently with IDE refactoring tools.

description: Numeric or string literals embedded directly in logic without explanation.
detection_signal: if status == 3:; timeout = 86400; MAX_ITEMS = 50 defined inline
why_bad: The meaning of the number is not obvious. When the value needs to change, it must be hunted throughout the code.
fix: Replace literals with named constants: MAX_SESSION_TIMEOUT = 86400; PAYMENT_PENDING_STATUS = 3.

description: Code with excessive indentation levels (4+ levels of if/for/try blocks).
detection_signal: Indentation > 4 levels; arrow-head shaped code; deeply nested try-except blocks
why_bad: Deep nesting is hard to read, test, and debug. The full execution path is difficult to trace.
fix: Apply early return / guard clauses to flatten the code. Extract deeply nested blocks into separate functions.

description: Code that calls operations that can fail (I/O, network, parsing) without handling the error case.
detection_signal: File open without try/except; network call with no timeout or error handling; JSON parse without catch
why_bad: Unhandled errors crash the process or leave it in an undefined state, potentially corrupting data.
fix: Wrap failure-prone operations in try/except. Handle specific exceptions. Log the error and fail gracefully.

description: An exception is caught but silently ignored — the catch block is empty or just contains a comment.
detection_signal: except Exception: pass; catch (Exception e) {}; try { ... } catch {}
why_bad: Silent failures make debugging extremely difficult. The code continues in a broken state with no indication of what went wrong.
fix: At minimum, log the exception. Better: handle it properly, or let it propagate to a handler that can.
source_label: Code smell: Empty Catch / Swallowed Exception

description: Code that dereferences a value that could be null/None without checking first.
detection_signal: Method called on result of .find(), .get(), or API call without null check; optional chaining missing
why_bad: NullPointerException / AttributeError crashes at runtime in production, often in an unrelated-looking location.
fix: Check for None before use, use Optional types with explicit handling, or use the Null Object pattern.

description: A Python function uses a mutable object (list, dict) as a default parameter value.
detection_signal: def append_item(item, lst=[]): or def update_config(cfg={}):
why_bad: The default object is created once at function definition time and shared across all calls. Mutations persist between calls.
fix: Use None as default and create the mutable object inside the function: if lst is None: lst = []

description: A loop executes a database query on each iteration instead of fetching all needed data in a single query.
detection_signal: db.query() inside a for loop; ORM lazy-loading accessed inside a loop
why_bad: For N items, N+1 database round trips are made instead of 1. Causes severe performance degradation at scale.
fix: Use a JOIN or IN query to fetch all related data in one call. Use ORM eager loading (select_related/prefetch_related).

description: URLs, file paths, timeouts, or environment-specific values hardcoded in source files instead of being configurable.
detection_signal: 'http://localhost:5432'; '/var/log/app.log' hardcoded; timeout = 30 embedded in business logic
why_bad: Changing the value requires modifying and redeploying code. Different environments need different values.
fix: Move all configuration to environment variables or a config file. Use sensible defaults but allow overrides.

description: Abstract base classes, factory patterns, or strategy objects introduced where a simple function would suffice.
detection_signal: Interface with a single implementation; factory that creates only one type of object; strategy with one strategy
why_bad: Unnecessary abstraction adds cognitive overhead and indirection without delivering flexibility.
fix: YAGNI — implement the simplest thing that works. Add the abstraction when the second variant actually appears.

description: Function or API handler that processes user input without validating type, range, or format first.
detection_signal: Direct use of request.args, req.body, or argv without schema validation or type coercion
why_bad: Unvalidated input causes crashes on unexpected types, silent data corruption, and security vulnerabilities.
fix: Validate and coerce input at the boundary (Pydantic, marshmallow, Joi, etc.) before passing it to business logic.

description: Shared mutable state accessed from multiple threads or async tasks without locks or atomic operations.
detection_signal: Global or instance variable read-modify-write outside a lock; counter++ in a threaded context; asyncio shared state without asyncio.Lock
why_bad: Non-atomic operations on shared state produce corrupted values under concurrent load. Intermittent and hard to reproduce.
fix: Use threading.Lock, asyncio.Lock, atomic operations, or queue-based message passing to coordinate shared state.

description: A test function that executes code but never calls assert, expect, or similar — it only tests that the code doesn't throw.
detection_signal: def test_foo(): obj = Foo(); obj.run()  # no assert statement
why_bad: The test will always pass even when the code is broken. It creates false confidence.
fix: Add at least one assertion that verifies the expected output or state after the operation.

description: Tests that depend on a large shared fixture, making it impossible to run a single test in isolation.
detection_signal: All tests in a class depend on a setUp that inserts 50+ records; test failure depends on insertion order
why_bad: Shared fixtures make tests slow, fragile, and order-dependent. A failure in setUp breaks all tests in the class.
fix: Use factory functions to create only the data each test needs. Prefer test isolation over shared state.
